questions.question: What does call f do?
options: Pushes return address, jumps to f
questions.explanation: Return address on top is how ret finds home.

questions.question: pushq %rbp; movq %rsp,%rbp does what?
options: Saves caller anchor, anchors this frame
questions.explanation: Classic prologue: preserve old rbp, set new anchor.

questions.question: Deeper calls have ___ %rsp?
questions.explanation: x86 stacks grow toward zero; depth sampler proves it.

questions.question: leave equals?
questions.explanation: Tear down frame then ret pops home.

questions.question: bt shows main -> frame_add. What is each line?
options: One live frame with its return address
questions.explanation: Backtrace = chain of frames linked via saved rbp/return addr.

questions.question: Why does -O2 -fomit-frame-pointer hinder bt?
options: Fuses/omits rbp anchors for speed; rsp-relative addressing instead
questions.explanation: Faster but less walkable; OS entry paths often keep frames.
